stt_sample.source: synthesized from STT_TEXT via Piper en_US-lessac-medium

legs.notes: piper-tts 1.7.0, new PiperVoice API. espeak-ng data bundled in wheel; no external espeak needed. RTF well under 1 (6-10x faster than realtime). Streams sentence-by-sentence so first-audio is one-sentence latency. WAVs: out/piper_short.wav, piper_medium.wav, piper_long.wav.

kokoro-onnx 0.6.1. G2P worked out-of-the-box: espeakng-loader bundles the espeak-ng binary + phonemizer 3.4.0, no separate espeak install needed. RTF > 1 (SLOWER than real-time) on this CPU with the int8 ONNX. CAVEAT: int8 Kokoro ONNX is widely reported slower than fp32 on CPU due to dynamic quantize/dequantize (QDQ) overhead without matching int8 kernels; fp32 comparison pending. first_audio measured via create_stream (async) and is very high because each streamed chunk is a full clause and int8 inference is slow. sample_rate 24000. WAVs: out/kokoro_short.wav, kokoro_medium.wav, kokoro_long.wav.

fp32 re-test confirming the int8 QDQ-overhead hypothesis: fp32 is ~2x FASTER than int8 on this CPU (short 0.87 vs 1.74; medium 0.59 vs 1.37). fp32 is real-time-capable (RTF<1) for medium/long but short is borderline (0.87) and it is still ~5-8x slower than Piper. Takeaway: for Kokoro on CPU use fp32, not int8. Model 325MB vs 92MB. long not re-run (bounded). WAVs: out/kokoro_fp32_short.wav, kokoro_fp32_medium.wav.

faster-whisper 1.2.1 / ctranslate2 4.8.2 (CPU-only, as expected - no CUDA). beam_size=5. Transcription quality essentially perfect on the clean synthesized sample. RTF ~0.94 (small) and ~1.13 (turbo) MEASURED UNDER HEAVY BACKGROUND CPU LOAD (box CPU ~97%, many node/MCP processes running); per-run variance was large (small: 0.81->1.05 across identical runs), so these are CONSERVATIVE. A dedicated run and/or greedy decoding (beam_size=1) would be materially faster. load_ms includes first-run model download+init. models cached in models/fw.

sherpa-onnx 1.x, OfflineRecognizer.from_transducer(model_type='nemo_transducer', greedy_search). RTF 0.17 = ~5-6x faster than real-time on CPU, EVEN under the same heavy background load that slowed faster-whisper. Transcript essentially perfect. This is the standout CPU STT result: real-time STT on CPU with NO NPU/GPU needed. Fed 16kHz mono (resampled from the 22.05kHz Piper sample via ffmpeg). Bundle 487MB compressed / ~670MB on disk (encoder.int8 652MB dominates).

legs.device_verification: core.available_devices=['CPU','GPU','NPU']; names: CPU='Intel Core Ultra 7 268V', GPU='Intel Arc 140V GPU (16GB) iGPU', NPU='Intel AI Boost'. WhisperPipeline(device) compiles per-device and throws on failure - it did not; all three produced identical, correct transcripts, confirming genuine on-device execution (no silent CPU fallback).
legs.notes: THE FINICKY LEG WORKED CLEANLY on all 3 devices - no driver/ABI/static-shape errors. Per-inference speed: NPU fastest (RTF 0.019, ~52x realtime), GPU next (0.024, ~42x), CPU (0.073, ~14x). BUT one-time compile cost is the catch: NPU 26.5s, GPU 18.1s, CPU 1.4s. For a 29s clip: CPU 2.1s vs NPU 0.55s inference - the accelerators save ~1.5s/clip but only pay off if the pipeline stays resident (compile amortized). whisper-base is a smaller model than the faster-whisper small/turbo tested in Leg 3, so cross-leg RTF is not apples-to-apples; within this leg the device comparison is clean (same model, back-to-back). Downloaded pre-converted IR (no torch export needed).

legs.sample: EN: The team finished the project yesterday. -> DE: Das Team hat das Projekt gestern beendet.
legs.notes: Pre-converted CT2 model, NO torch installed (ctranslate2 already present from faster-whisper; only sentencepiece added). Two pitfalls resolved: (1) MarianMT requires '</s>' APPENDED to the source token list - without it the decoder never emits EOS and degenerates into repetitive garbage while decoding to the 256-token max (~6s/sentence); appending '</s>' fixed correctness AND cut latency to ~95ms. (2) Windows cp1252 stdout raised UnicodeEncodeError on the sentencepiece marker char and on German umlauts - run with PYTHONUTF8=1. Latency is single-sentence (batch=1); batched throughput would be far higher. 95ms/sentence single-threaded-ish (4 threads) is easily fast enough for live per-sentence translation.
